# `scope_set_track_state`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Turn the mount's sidereal tracking on or off.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build: C / MUTATOR established independently, full contract parity unresolved) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x71c50 (64-bit guider build); driver SetTrackState @0xf18e0; 32-bit handler @0x6c818 |

Requires a connected mount that supports tracking control. The driver writes the track-on or track-off command to the controller and checks the response characters. Whether that succeeds or not, the handler then runs a forced tracking-state check, which updates shared tracking status and can emit a ScopeTrack event (members include state, tracking and manual, with a conditional error, code and route). The success fragment is built before that check and the event can precede the reply; ordering is not established. The reply is sent synchronously after the controller acknowledgment, with no long-running wait. Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): :Te or :Td; with mount firmware 1.1.0 or later :GAT follows and maps e5# to 270, e7# to 502, e8# to 272, e13# to 527, other e..# to 207.

Side effects: Writes the track-on or track-off command to the mount controller, updates shared tracking status and may emit a ScopeTrack event.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_set_track_state"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | yes | - | Required. A bare boolean, the first element of an array, or an object {tracking}. The parser unwraps the first array element and selects the member tracking when that element is an object; the Android app sends a bare boolean. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 106 | The tracking value is not a boolean or an integer | `expected bool param` |
| 210 | The mount or its driver does not support tracking control | `not supported` |
| 315 | No mount is connected | `mount is not connected` |
| 270 | Tracking-reason query replied e5# | `below horizon` |
| 502 | Tracking-reason query replied e7# | `mount sync failed` |
| 272 | Tracking-reason query replied e8# | `meridian flip failed` |
| 527 | Tracking-reason query replied e13# | `alt exceed limit` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

When the driver reports failure the handler forwards its error code. Further branches forward an error code set by the mount driver or a helper; the codes are not exhausted by this table.

## Example

Request, scalar - Bare boolean, as the app sends it:

```json
{"id":61,"method":"scope_set_track_state","params":true}
```

Request, named:

```json
{"id":62,"method":"scope_set_track_state","params":{"tracking":false}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_track_state","result":0,"code":0,"id":61}
```

Reply, no-mount:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_track_state","error":"mount is not connected","code":315,"id":63}
```
